meta.title: Telemavix - GPS tracks and telemetry overlays for action cameras | Sefinek
meta.description: Record GPS tracks on your phone and add speed, maps and other data to action camera and drone footage. Discover Telemavix GPS and Telemavix Studio.
meta.keywords: telemavix, telemetry overlay, gps track, fit, gpx, dji osmo action, gopro, dji drone, hud

softwareDescription: Telemavix GPS records routes and phone sensor data. Telemavix Studio adds overlays with speed, maps, tilt and other readings to your videos.
label: Project
heading: Telemavix
intro: Your footage can show more. Choose from over 40 widgets in Telemavix Studio, from maps and speedometers to heart rate and flight data. Use data from the original MP4 of a supported camera or drone, a FIT or GPX track, or a DJI flight log. Use Telemavix GPS to record your route and phone sensor readings. With an Osmo Action 4, 5 Pro or 6, the app can replace the DJI Osmo Action GPS Bluetooth Remote Controller. One button starts logging and filming, and the camera saves GPS positions in its MP4 file.

how.title: How to add telemetry to a video

steps.title: 1. Record your activity
steps.text: Film your activity with an action camera or drone. Use Telemavix GPS alongside it if you want a separate route file or readings from your phone sensors.

steps.title: 2. Open the footage in Studio
steps.text: Start with the original camera file. If it contains telemetry, Studio reads it directly from the footage. You can also add a FIT or GPX file from your phone, sports watch or bike computer. If your DJI drone records telemetry separately, add the DJI flight log.

steps.title: 3. Add an overlay and save your video
steps.text: If you use a separate telemetry file, check that it lines up with the video. Choose your widgets, arrange them on the footage and check the preview before exporting.

apps.title: From GPS track to video overlay

mobile.title: Telemavix GPS for Android
mobile.text: Record your route and phone sensor readings during an activity, even with the screen off.

highlights.title: Use your phone as an Osmo Action GPS remote
highlights.text: Connect an Osmo Action 4, 5 Pro or 6 over Bluetooth. Start filming and logging with one button. The camera saves your phone's GPS positions in the original MP4.

highlights.title: Live readings and activity history
highlights.text: Check speed, distance, elevation gain and grade. After your activity, revisit the route map and charts or open the FIT or GPX recording in Studio.

screens.dashboard: Telemavix GPS dashboard showing speed, distance, elapsed time and grade.
screens.camera: Camera recording settings in Telemavix GPS showing GPS forwarding to a DJI camera and linked recording.

desktop.title: Telemavix Studio
desktop.text: Edit footage from your action camera or drone and show what happened along the route or during the flight.
desktop.alt: Telemavix Studio workspace with footage from a forest trail, a map, a speedometer, the widget panel and the timeline.

screens.speed: The Default, Modern, Ring and Legacy speedometers all show 22 km/h on the same country road.
screens.route: Bridge crossing with an aerial map and GPS trail, a compass, and the ride's elevation profile.

highlights.title: Telemetry from the original MP4
highlights.text: Studio reads data from supported cameras and drones. You can also add a FIT or GPX track or a DJI flight log. Align an external track with the footage and use a second sync point to correct clock drift.

highlights.title: Over 40 widgets in the live preview
highlights.text: Place a map, tilt indicator, heart rate or flight readings on the video. Save your layout as a preset and use the timeline to choose when widgets appear.

highlights.title: Export the overlay on its own
highlights.text: Join and trim clips in Studio or export the widgets with a transparent background to layer them over footage in another editor.

download.title: Download Telemavix Studio
download.intro: Choose a package for your operating system and processor. On Windows, the installer is the simplest option. The current version is {{version}}.
download.cpuHelp: Not sure which processor you have? On Windows, go to Settings > System > About and check System type. On Linux and macOS, run `uname -m`: x86_64 means x64, while arm64 or aarch64 means ARM64.
download.runtimeHelp: If you choose the version that requires .NET, install the [.NET 10 Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) for your system and processor. Studio also needs FFmpeg 9 and offers to install it on first launch if it is missing. Linux and macOS versions are experimental.
download.more: All files, checksums and release notes are on the [releases page]({{releasesUrl}}).

devices.title: Supported cameras, drones and Garmin devices
devices.intro: Find your device to see whether the original footage has the data you need or whether to add a GPS track or flight log.
devices.note: If your camera does not record GPS, track your route on your phone with [Telemavix GPS](#apps) and add it to Studio as a FIT or GPX file. See the [camera telemetry guide](#camera-telemetry) for details.

rows.notes: Studio uses accelerometer readings to calculate roll, pitch and G-force. It also reads ISO and shutter speed from the MP4. Tested with the Osmo Action 5 Pro and 6.
rows.gps: Open the original MP4. It contains GPS positions if the camera received them from Telemavix GPS or a DJI GPS Bluetooth remote while filming.

rows.notes: Studio reads position, speed and height above takeoff, among other flight data.
rows.gps: The Lito X1 Plus embeds the data in its MP4. For the Mavic Air 2, Mavic 4 Pro, Flip and Avata 360, add the flight log (FlightRecord_*.txt) from your phone or remote controller.

rows.notes: Studio reads motion and exposure data from the footage. Pitch readings were checked on HERO12 Black footage.
rows.gps: The HERO12 Black has no built-in GPS. Add a GPS track from the Telemavix GPS app, a sports watch or a bike computer.

rows.notes: Studio also reads heart rate, cadence and battery level when present. FIT import was tested with the Garmin 7X.
rows.gps: Open the FIT activity file from your Garmin watch or bike computer.

rows.notes: Studio reads tilt and G-force data and lets you reframe 360° footage. Other Insta360 cameras are unsupported.
rows.gps: The X4 has no built-in GPS. Add a FIT or GPX track in Studio, for example from a phone or sports watch.
